s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Lesions symmetrically distributed and ranging from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: 2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round and hypopigmented
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions range from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
No hair growth at site of lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with congenital or acquired hypopigmented lesions

shortlist.label: Vitiligo
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given hypopigmented macules, although typically accompanied by symptoms

shortlist.label: Pityriasis alba
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to hypopigmented patches, but usually associated with mild scaling

shortlist.label: Nevus of Ito
shortlist.why_kept: Matches description of hypopigmented macules, although typically presents with other features

trace.fact: Lesion onset: 2 years prior to presentation
Lesion size: 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Previous treatment: tinea versicolor treatment, without success
Skin feature: absence of hair growth at the site of the lesions
Histopathologic finding: neoplastic cords with clear/pale epithelial cells
Cell characteristic: strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation
Dermis characteristic: marked elastosis surrounding tumor
